properties.description: The validity envelope, as one or more role/dimension/value statements. FP-WF1 alone needs three at once (trained-on/spatial, valid-for/ecological, can-run-on/climatic) — see `envelopeConstraint` for why role and dimension are independent axes.

Position array, nested per `type` as RFC 7946 §3.1 defines it (e.g. a `Polygon`'s coordinates are an array of linear rings, each an array of `[lon, lat]` positions). Left as `array` here rather than spelling out all four `type`-specific shapes, since JSON Schema can't easily key a nested shape off a sibling `enum` value without substantially more structure than a small, evidence-seeded constraint value needs.
Start of the interval. Granularity is workflow-specific (a date, a year, a multi-year period) and not constrained here.
End of the interval, same granularity as `start`.
A non-calendar, scenario-indexed temporal position (e.g. a Global Warming Level label) where no calendar interval can be stated.
Which aspect of the envelope this statement describes.
Which axis of variation this statement constrains. Open vocabulary, seeded deliberately small — expect WF-owner review to surface dimensions not yet listed here.

The constraint value itself, shaped by `dimension`:
- `spatial`/`jurisdictional` — a real geographic/administrative extent, since text throws
  away exactly the thing this envelope model exists to support: an automated check like
  "does my AOI fall inside this workflow's `valid-for` area?" cannot be answered against a
  free-text label. `value` **must** be a GeoJSON Geometry (RFC 7946 §3.1: `Point`,
  `MultiPoint`, `Polygon`, or `MultiPolygon` — the shapes evidenced so far;
  `LineString`/`MultiLineString`/`GeometryCollection` can be added later if evidence needs
  them), even an approximate one (e.g. UP-WF2's EURO-CORDEX domain, rendered as its published
  bounding box) — not just permitted, since text is not a fallback for "haven't looked up the
  coordinates yet." A workflow with a genuinely unlocatable `spatial`/`jurisdictional` fact
  (no resolvable source location at all) should omit that envelope entry, or use
  `transferability/notes`' `transferabilityNotes` on a sibling fact to record the caveat in
  prose, rather than smuggling free text into `value`.
- `temporal` — the calendar span, or non-calendar scenario marker, results are valid over.
  `value` is either `{start, end}` (a plain calendar interval; granularity is
  workflow-specific — a date, a year, a multi-year period — and not constrained here) or
  `{scenarioMarker}` (a non-calendar, scenario-indexed position, e.g. a Global Warming Level
  label like `GWL+1.5`, for results that genuinely aren't calendar-indexed — a warming level
  is reached at different years depending on emissions scenario/ensemble member). A workflow
  with no fixed window at all (e.g. an ongoing sensor observation) should omit the entry
  rather than fabricate one.
- `ecological`/`climatic` — the vocabulary's other two seeded dimension terms, neither a
  literal extent or interval — `value` stays plain `string`, since "a comparable ecological
  range" doesn't become more machine-readable by wrapping it in coordinates it doesn't have.
- Any dimension term outside all four above — the vocabulary is open, so a term not yet
  seeded here is still allowed — falls back to plain `string` too, until evidence shows it
  needs its own structured shape.

Four `oneOf` branches, not three: `ecological`/`climatic` get their own branch, listed by name, distinct from the catch-all for a genuinely new, not-yet-seeded dimension term — even though both branches currently validate `value` the same way (`string`). Keeping them apart makes each currently-known dimension term traceable to an explicit branch instead of only being defined by negation, and means that if a future known term (`ecological`, say) turns out to need its own structured `value` shape, it moves to a new named branch without disturbing what "not yet classified" means for everything else.
No existing OGC Block carries a bare GeoJSON Geometry union standalone: `ogc.geo.common.data_types.geojson` (the main OGC register's stable GeoJSON block) only exposes this shape nested inside a full `Feature` wrapper (`type`/`properties`/`geometry`), no `$defs` fragment for just the geometry union — checked its actual schema, not assumed — which is heavier than a constraint value needs and isn't `$ref`-able as a bare fragment. This repo's own `forestStandFeature` hits the same wall (wraps the full `ogc.geo.features.feature` Feature shape, not a bare geometry), and no other register has one either. So, same posture as `qualityAnnotation` binding straight to DQV with no wrapping OGC Block to depend on, this binds directly to RFC 7946 rather than to a Feature-shaped block.

The reference/calibration artifacts and the rules governing how each must be adapted outside the validity envelope. Not every artifact a workflow depends on needs an entry here — only those with an evidenced transferability fact.
Free-text label identifying the reference or calibration artifact these rules apply to (e.g. "downscaled FOCAL climate data", "Quitt climate-zone thresholds/limits").

What kind of thing this artifact is, independent of whether a CWL id exists for it yet: `workflow-input` — consumed as a workflow input (a config file, parameter, or reference dataset); `workflow-output` — produced by (a step of) the workflow and reused as an input elsewhere, e.g. a trained model; `external-resource` — referenced by the workflow's documentation but not wired into its CWL graph, e.g. an optional validation dataset; `infrastructure` — physical or operational, not data at all, e.g. a sensor network that must be re-deployed rather than replaced.

The artifact's CWL id, as `inputs.<id>` or `outputs.<id>` of whatever `CWLWorkflow` this statement is attached to. Optional: only meaningful when `artifactRole` is `workflow-input` or `workflow-output`, and only fillable once a real CWL Application Package exists to bind against — omit otherwise rather than guess an id.
One or more condition/action rules governing this artifact.
Free-text elaboration of a transferability fact the controlled vocabulary can't capture, or of the consequence of an optional action being skipped (see transferability/rule's `required`).
The condition that triggers this rule.
One or more actions, any of which resolves `triggeredBy` — an OR-set, not a required combination (no evidenced case needs more than one action applied simultaneously).

Whether applying one of `actions` is mandatory once `triggeredBy` holds. Defaults to true. When false, skipping is allowed but degrades result quality/trust rather than blocking execution — describe the consequence in `transferabilityNotes`.
